description: Curated agreement cases: HQ rulings where CBP applied 19 CFR 102.20 and stated whether the tariff shift was met, and where the good's and materials' classifications are both determinable from the ruling text.
selection: Mechanical, then curated. Candidates are every HQ ruling citing 102.20 that (a) quotes a 102.20 rule, (b) states a shift verdict attributed to 102.11(a)(3) or 102.20 rather than to a preferential annex, and (c) states one polarity only. Each candidate was then read; those whose good or material codes are not stated were dropped, and every remaining one was kept regardless of whether originshift agrees with it.
dropped: 735554, 735588, H325232, W562873, 562012, 956420 (good or material classification not stated); H281296, H296462 (the matched sentence recites 102.13's de minimis provision rather than stating a finding)

country_cases: Where a case carries `origins` and `cbp_country`, the country CBP held is compared with the one the resolver reaches. Cases were excluded where the ruling covers several scenarios or products (H332368, H320969, 735447), where the essential-character material is commingled across countries so 102.11(b)(2) applies (H332368 scenario 2), where CBP reached the answer by a paragraph other than 102.11(b) (558944, 559431), and where the good is a set governed by 102.11(c) (560081).
